subject: Acme integration - rate limits & retries
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Acme integration - rate limits & retries

Thanks for the call today — great to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side regarding SDK/auth/routing and the rate-limits conversation: 

1) Integration items we agreed on:
- SDK: we'll send a Python and Node sample showing auth via API key and token refresh patterns.
- Routing: recommend per-route model selection (chat vs. embeddings) with a single API key; we can provide examples using request headers for "x-rw-route".
- Structured output/tool-calling: we will provide a JSON schema example and a short demo request showing function/tool calling.

2) Rate limiting and retries (summary):
- Quotas: Acme will start on "Standard" quota (200 reqs/minute, burst to 400 for 60s).
- 429 handling: client should implement exponential backoff with jitter; Redwood returns Retry-After when available.
- Idempotency: for any non-idempotent mutating calls (long running batching/feedback endpoints) include a client-generated request_id (UUID) in header "x-rw-request-id"; Redwood will store short-lived dedupe keys (5 minutes).

3) Embeddings / rerankers:
- Embedding calls are metered separately from generation tokens. We recommend batching vectorize calls (up to 128 items) and using our small-embeddings quantized models for cost.

Attachments: sending our internal Rate Limits playbook (PDF) + sample retry helper (Python) in follow-up.

Next steps: 
- Ben: share sample SDK snippets + attachments (today).
- Acme: confirm expected concurrency and peak qps so we can propose Dedicated pool if needed.
- Schedule follow-up call next week to review live demo + policy.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hey Ben — thanks for the notes and for the clear plan. A few clarifying questions from our infra/infra-ml side: 

- On 429s: if we receive a 429 on a streaming generation request (server-streaming tokens), should the client re-establish the stream and resume with the same request_id, or is the server expected to return a resumable token/offset?
- For idempotency keys: will Redwood reject a second request with the same request_id if the original is still in-flight, or will it dedupe and return the original response once complete? Trying to understand behavior during retries vs concurrent retries.
- Embeddings quotas: are embeddings counted by request (per call) or by vector count? We have micro-batching on our side but want to map to billing.

Also, can you share the sample SDK snippet showing how you suggest adding the request_id header and handling Retry-After?

Hi Liam — good questions. Short answers up front, then details: 

- Streaming + 429s: clients should re-open the stream with the same x-rw-request-id. For short interruptions, Redwood will attempt best-effort resume semantics for chat sessions (up to 30s) using server KV checkpoints, but we do not guarantee byte-level resume for arbitrary sequence numbers. For guaranteed resume you should checkpoint your request state client-side and replay with the same request_id.

- Idempotency behavior: if a second request arrives with a matching x-rw-request-id while the first is in-flight, Redwood will return HTTP 409 (duplicate-in-flight) to indicate "already processing". Once the original completes, a subsequent same-request_id will return the cached response (within 5 minutes). We surface a x-rw-idempotency-status header with values: accepted | duplicate-in-flight | replayed-from-cache.

- Embeddings billing: counted by vector elements returned (i.e., per item). A single embeddings.batch call returning N vectors counts as N embedding units. Batching reduces per-vector overhead but not the per-vector billing unit. We'll include rates in the attached playbook.

Attached is a minimal Python snippet for request_id + retry handling (see sample-retry-ids.py). Key points:
- Use exponential backoff with decorrelated jitter (base 200ms, max 8s).
- Respect Retry-After if present; use Retry-After over computed backoff in first retry window.
- Use Idempotency UUIDs for replayable requests (batch submissions, feedback events).

[Attachment: sample-retry-ids.py]

If helpful, Rishi can follow up with suggested per-route quotas and whether Dedicated capacity makes sense for your peak.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that helps. A couple more practical questions from our SDK team: 

- Could you provide the Node sample demonstrating how to set the x-rw-request-id header for both unary and streaming endpoints?
- For streaming, if the client gets a 409 duplicate-in-flight, should it poll for completion or subscribe to a callback/webhook? We are leaning toward polling for the first phase but want best practices.
- For embeddings/rerankers: does reranker throughput share the same token-rate quota as generation, or is it isolated? We plan to run reranking in-line after embeddings and want to avoid throttling cascades.

Happy to jump on a short tech call with Rishi and Marissa this week to walk through the sample code.

Appreciate the follow-ups — summary + attachments included.

Summary of final clarifications and action items: 

- Node + Python SDK samples: attached (sample-retry-ids.py includes Node equivalent inside comments and a link to the repo). Use header: headers['x-rw-request-id'] = uuid.v4(); for streaming prepend request metadata with same id.
- 409 duplicate-in-flight: recommended flow:
  - On 409, poll the status endpoint (GET /v1/requests/{request_id}/status) with exponential backoff for up to 60s.
  - If you prefer server notifications, we can open a webhook subscription for request completion (requires Dedicated/Private plans or support enablement).
- Streaming resume: treat server-side resume as best-effort. For strict resume you should checkpoint tokens client-side.
- Reranker/embeddings quotas: embeddings and reranker calls are billed and rate-limited separately from token-generation. However, overall account concurrency limits apply (total concurrent connections). If you expect bursts where both pipelines run in-line, we recommend enabling a dedicated pool or bumping concurrency caps.

Attached: redwood-rate-limits.pdf, sample-retry-ids.py, acme-multiplexing-plan.xlsx

Next steps: 
- Ben/Rishi: propose Dedicated sizing if Acme confirms peak QPS (please send numbers).
- Acme: share expected p95 concurrency and average embedding batch size.
- Schedule: I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 2026-02-25 for an SDK walk-through and live demo.

Thanks and talk soon,
